message.reasoning:
I need to make a Monopoly decision.

I'm p4 with $241 and the light blue monopoly at one house each. The opponent is p2 with $141, holding Baltic, orange, red, and dark blue monopolies. Only p2 remains.

The opponent also holds Short Line unmortgaged. I am at Electric Company and p2 at Indiana Avenue. I need to choose one post-turn action from end_turn, propose_trade, unmortgage_property, build_houses_or_hotel, or sell_houses_or_hotel.

I already rolled and landed on the mortgaged Electric Company. No rent is collected there. I am now choosing a post-turn action.

Trading is unwise. Completing monopolies for the opponent would help them, and the bank only has four houses left. Building or unmortgaging would waste cash on low returns. Selling my three houses would give the bank seven total.

Hotel construction returns four houses to the bank. The opponent can therefore build hotels on their orange properties without needing bank houses. House denial will not block them from upgrading.

I am calculating exact rent values to assess the opponent's threat. Orange hotels would charge $950 to $1050, while red hotels would charge $1050 to $1100. Dark blue properties are also being checked.

Dark blue properties charge $1100 to $1400 for three houses. That would instantly bankrupt me.

The opponent has $141 cash. Hotel construction on an orange property costs only $100 and returns four houses. After that, St James would charge $950.

I am checking whether the opponent has uneven house counts on their dark blue properties.

The opponent cannot build on dark blue or red properties right now. Dark blue needs $200 per house, and red needs $150 each. Their $141 cash is too low for even one house. They would need to mortgage something to proceed.

Mortgaging Baltic for $30 would give the opponent $171, enough to build one red house. That is not an immediate threat. I am now considering whether building my light blue properties to two houses would help me kill them.

Building two houses on all three light blue properties costs $150, leaving me with $91. Two-house rents would still be manageable for the opponent. Building to three houses would require another $150, but I only have $241, so that is impossible. I can only afford to raise every property by one house.

The bank has four houses available. I can raise every light blue property by one house for $150, leaving $91. I could also build two houses on two properties and one on the third for $200, which is still within my budget.

Building three houses on Connecticut would charge $300 in rent. The opponent has $141 cash, so they would need to raise $159. They could mortgage Baltic for $30 and Short Line for $100 to cover that gap. Selling houses would only recover half their original cost.

The opponent's total liquidation value is enormous. Their houses alone are worth roughly $1,725. They could sell them to cover a $300 Connecticut rent without going bankrupt. Light blue rents cannot kill them unless they are already cash-poor. I cannot bankrupt the opponent with these properties.

I am weighing whether forcing the opponent to sell houses is worth the cash I would spend. Downgrading their properties reduces their rent power, but it also costs me money while I need to survive their upcoming landings.

I am reviewing the board layout to plan my next move. Electric Company sits between St. Charles and States Avenue, so I will land on one of those properties after rolling.

Rolling 2 through 4 from Electric Company lands on States, Virginia, and Pennsylvania Railroad. All three are either my own mortgaged properties or the opponent's mortgaged spaces, so they pose no rent threat. The first dangerous landing is a roll of 5, which would hit St. James with four houses for $750.

Rolling 5, 7, or 8 from Electric Company would hit the opponent's orange properties for $750, $800, and $850. That is a death roll unless I can raise those houses first. Rolling 10 or 12 lands on red properties for $250 each, which I can afford. I am calculating whether I can pay the orange rent by selling one house from each light blue property for $75, or by mortgaging all three for $160.

I cannot afford the orange rent. My maximum raise is $476, which is below the $750 St. James charge. Selling houses now does not generate more cash than selling later. I will preserve my options and avoid wasting money.

I am now considering whether building houses on my light blues would force the opponent to sell houses before they can hotel. Hotel construction costs only $100, so they could still build hotels with their current cash. Since four-house orange rent already kills me, upgrading will not change my survival odds. I am also weighing whether any trade could help me avoid those dangerous landings or raise enough cash.

I need $274 more liquidity to survive the orange rent. Trading States Avenue for their pink monopoly would not help, since they already hold St. Charles and Virginia and that trade would give them more kill squares.

I am now evaluating other trade offers. Ventnor would complete the yellow monopoly, but that would add more death squares rather than help me survive. Mediterranean would complete brown with Baltic, yet brown is too weak to save me from orange. Water Works would give them a utility pair, though they would need to unmortgage Electric Company first. Pacific and North Carolina would complete the green monopoly, which is deadly.

Railroad monopolies are not viable trade targets because neither side owns a full set. I cannot force the opponent to sell houses through a trade, and they would never trade their orange properties with four houses for cash.

I considered offering a large cash payment to survive the orange rent, but the opponent has only $141 and would need to mortgage or sell assets to pay me. They would not give away survival money when they can simply wait for me to land on orange and win.

I will keep my houses as emergency liquidity for the upcoming red rent of $250. Building now would waste cash I might need for that charge. Unmortgaging Mediterranean is a poor idea because it costs $33 to unmortgage and yields only $2 or $4 in rent without a monopoly. Reading Railroad unmortgages for $110, which is slightly more than its $100 mortgage value.

Unmortgaging any of my mortgaged properties would cost more than the rent they generate. Reading Railroad and Pennsylvania Railroad each cost $110 to unmortgage for only $25 in rent. States Avenue, Ventnor Avenue, and Water Works are similarly poor deals. Pacific Avenue costs $165 to unmortgage for just $40 in rent. None of these options are worth the cash.

I will end my turn. Selling houses now would give me $316, but I am checking whether that extra cash could fund any other move.

I checked the opponent's next possible landings from Indiana Avenue. They will not land on any of my light blue properties, so selling my houses now would lose rent opportunities without preventing a future orange hit.
